1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:20. Alternate translation: [During his reign]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:3. Alternate translation: [came] or [invaded]

The author is speaking as if Jehoiakim had been away somewhere and **returned**. He means that he decided to become a vassal of Egypt once again and so stopped serving Nebuchadnezzar. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Then he resumed his previous loyalty to Egypt]

2.note: The term **Chaldeans** is another name for the people group also known as Babylonians. If you have decided to use the same names in your translation that the biblical author does in each place, you may wish to use the name Chaldeans here. If you have decided to use the same names for people and groups throughout your translation, you may wish to use the name Babylonians here.
See how you translated the similar expression in [1:1](ta:01). Alternate translation: [and raiding bands of Arameans and raiding bands of Moabites]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:12. Alternate translation: [Ammonites]
Since the author has already used the name Yahweh earlier in this verse, it may be more natural in your language to use a pronoun here. Alternate translation: [according to his word]
See how you translated the similar expression in 9:36. Alternate translation: [through the agency of his servants the prophets]

3.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 23:35. Alternate translation: [to fulfill what Yahweh had said]

The author is speaking in a way that is characteristic of his culture by using a feminine verb, **it was**, to refer to a general situation. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [this came upon Judah] or [all of this happened to Judah]
See how you translated the similar expression in 13:23. Alternate translation: [away from their land]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 21:16. Alternate translation: [because he had killed many innocent people]
See how you translated the similar expression in 21:16. Alternate translation: [for he had killed innocent people violently in every part of Jerusalem]

5.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יְהוֹיָקִ֖ים וְ⁠כָל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲ⁠לֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה
5.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is concluding the story of Jehoiakim. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

6.note: See how you translated the same expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [And Jehoiakim passed away] or [And Jehoiakim died]

7.q: וְ⁠לֹֽא־הֹסִ֥יף עוֹד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לָ⁠צֵ֖את מֵֽ⁠אַרְצ֑⁠וֹ כִּֽי־לָקַ֞ח מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֗ל מִ⁠נַּ֤חַל מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ עַד־נְהַר־פְּרָ֔ת כֹּ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיְתָ֖ה לְ⁠מֶ֥לֶךְ מִצְרָֽיִם
7.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And since the king of Babylon took all that had been to the king of Egypt from the wadi of Egypt to the Euphrates River the king of Egypt did not resume again to go out from his land]

7.q: וְ⁠לֹֽא־הֹסִ֥יף עוֹד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לָ⁠צֵ֖את מֵֽ⁠אַרְצ֑⁠וֹ
7.note: It might seem that the expression **did not resume again** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [And the king of Egypt did not go out from his land anymore]

8.q: בֶּן־שְׁמֹנֶ֨ה עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין בְּ⁠מָלְכ֔⁠וֹ וּ⁠שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה חֳדָשִׁ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ⁠ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ⁠שֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔⁠וֹ נְחֻשְׁתָּ֥א בַת־אֶלְנָתָ֖ן מִ⁠ירוּשָׁלִָֽם
8.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Jehoiachin** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:26.

9.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:2. Alternate translation: [And he did what Yahweh considered to be evil]

10.note: The author is using **entered into siege** as a common expression of his culture to mean that the **servants of Nebuchadnezzar** (his military commanders) besieged the city. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the city came under siege] or [and they besieged the city]

12.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:25. Alternate translation: [in the eighth year of his reign]

13.q: אֶת־כָּל־אוֹצְרוֹת֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְ⁠אֽוֹצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית הַ⁠מֶּ֑לֶךְ
13.note: The plural form **treasuries** suggests that these terms represent the valuable items that were in the treasury of each building. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [all of the valuable items that were in the treasury of the house of Yahweh and the treasury of the house of the king]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:18. Alternate translation: [the temple of Yahweh]

As the use of the verb translated as **cut off** in 16:17 and 18:16 indicates, the author means that Nebuchadnezzar had his men cut the **gold** off of these **furnishings**. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and he cut the gold off all of the furnishings]

14.q: וְ⁠הִגְלָ֣ה אֶת־כָּל־יְ֠רוּשָׁלִַם וְֽ⁠אֶת־כָּל־הַ⁠שָּׂרִ֞ים וְ⁠אֵ֣ת ׀ כָּל־גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י הַ⁠חַ֗יִל עשרה אֲלָפִים֙ גּוֹלֶ֔ה וְ⁠כָל־הֶ⁠חָרָ֖שׁ וְ⁠הַ⁠מַּסְגֵּ֑ר
14.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **every craftsman and smith** with the information about the **commanders** and **warriors**. Alternate translation: [And he exiled all of Jerusalem and all of the commanders and all of the mighty of valor and every craftsman and smith, exiling 10,000]

14.q: וְ⁠הִגְלָ֣ה אֶת־כָּל־יְ֠רוּשָׁלִַם וְֽ⁠אֶת־כָּל־הַ⁠שָּׂרִ֞ים וְ⁠אֵ֣ת ׀ כָּל־גִּבּוֹרֵ֣י הַ⁠חַ֗יִל & וְ⁠כָל־הֶ⁠חָרָ֖שׁ וְ⁠הַ⁠מַּסְגֵּ֑ר
14.note: By **all of Jerusalem**, the author means everyone in the city in the categories he then describes. In other words, the phrases that follow limit the meaning of that phrase. Alternate translation: [And he exiled all of Jerusalem, that is, all of the commanders and all of the mighty of valor and every craftsman and smith] or [And he exiled all of the commanders and the mighty of valor and every craftsman and smith from Jerusalem]

While this expression can describe great soldiers, that does not seem to be the meaning in this context. The author says in verse 16 that the Babylonians exiled 7,000 such people, and the Judean army would have had many more great soldiers than that. So the meaning seems instead to be the same as in 15:20, that these were wealthy and powerful citizens. See how you translated the expression there in order to determine how to translate it here and the similar one in verse 16 (“the men of valor”). Alternate translation: [the wealthy citizens]

The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language, here and in verse 16. Alternate translation: [10,000 people]

If it would appear in your language that the author was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [The only ones left were the poor of the people of the land]

The author is using the adjective **poor** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the poor people who lived in the land]

16.note: The author is not referring to a specific **craftsman** or **smith**. He means those workers in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and the craftsmen and the smiths]

This seems to be a summary statement of all the categories of people listed in verses 14–16 whom the Babylonians took into exile. The idea seems to be that Nebuchadnezzar exiled all the Judeans who together could have made **war** against him. Alternate translation: [all those who together had the capacity to make war against him]

17.note: The pronoun **his** refers to Jehoiachin, not to Nebuchadnezzar, the **king of Babylon**. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [Jehoiachin’s uncle]
See how you indicated the symbolic significance of this action in 23:34.

18.q: בֶּן־עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְ⁠אַחַ֤ת שָׁנָה֙ צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ בְ⁠מָלְכ֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠אַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּ⁠ירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְ⁠שֵׁ֣ם אִמּ֔⁠וֹ חמיטל בַּֽת־יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ מִ⁠לִּבְנָֽה
18.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is introducing **Zedekiah** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:26.
